notes:
Copilot runs foreground subagents IN-PROCESS: subagent.started/subagent.completed pair on toolCallId inside the parent's events.jsonl and no session-state/<child>/ directory is ever created. So the claudecode/opencode phase shape (child_session_birth as transcript_new + parent_linked) is not merely absent here, it is unreachable — there is no child SessionState to link. What this spec CAN assert is the arc the scenario's process section actually turns on: the parent goes ready→working at spawn, is HELD working across the child's lifetime (both subagent events are Skip=true in parser.go:390, and Copilot's only turn boundary is the explicit assistant.turn_end), and returns working→ready only after the subagent has completed. KNOWN FAILING, and NOT expressible as a phase: SubagentCount(parent) must read 1 between the two subagent events, but agents.SubagentCounters (maps.go:137-153) closes over a parser instance created at wiring time while the metrics adapter tails with a different per-transcript instance (adapter.go:78-86, :123), so session.SessionMetrics.OpenSubagents is always 0 — probe through the real collector seen red at 'domain OpenSubagents = 0, want 1'. expected.jsonl's DSL matches only state_transition states and lifecycle kinds and ObservationSpec covers model/cost/tokens, so there is no predicate for a subagent count; the flag plus the assessment body are the record of the broken half, and the phases below deliberately assert the CORRECT behaviour of the half that works. Single-birth adapter (agent.FilesUnderRoot + sessionIDFromPath keys the session to its session-state/<id>/ dir), so the birth is one phase anchored to start UNPINNED. duration_at_least_ms on the working phase is what bounds the held-working invariant window — 5000ms is a floor chosen well under a realistic gpt-5-mini subagent span, not the span itself. model is left unpinned (--model accepts only "auto"; the effective model is resolved at runtime via session.auto_mode_resolved) and cost is unasserted (gpt-5-mini has no core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go entry) — record fills both from the recording.

KNOWN_FAILING CLEARED 2026-08-05 (CLI 1.0.78) — BY A LIVE PROBE, because this cell's defect is in a metric the recorded events.jsonl does not carry. The frozen verdict was daemon=bug: the parser counted subagents correctly but agents.SubagentCounters built ONE parser at wiring time and closed over it, while the metrics Adapter builds a SEPARATE parser per transcript path (parserFor, from ComputeMetrics) — so the closed-over instance never consumed a line and any adapter keeping its count in parser state reported zero forever. Claude Code was immune by accident, not design: its CountOpenSubagents ignores the receiver, so it reads identically from a stale instance, and its own unit test passed for that same reason. Copilot is the first adapter to keep the count in parser state and therefore the first victim. Fixed in 00af8004, pinned red-first by TestCountOpenSubagents_UsesTheParserThatActuallyParsed.

THE LIVE EVIDENCE (polling GET /api/v1/sessions once a second against the recording daemon during a real three-way fan-out on 2026-08-05):
  proc-30684   ready    open_subagents=-   last=-
  6f6288fa-af4 working  open_subagents=-   last=turn_start
  6f6288fa-af4 working  open_subagents=3   last=function_call
  6f6288fa-af4 working  open_subagents=3   last=user_message
  6f6288fa-af4 working  open_subagents=3   last=function_call_output
  6f6288fa-af4 ready    open_subagents=-   last=turn_done
The parent reports three open in-process children for the whole span and drops back to zero on turn_done. Under the old wiring this column read 0 at every sample. BIRTH RE-ANCHORED: the real session is born directly into `working` (commit 3cde4f8d), so session_birth and turn_start_held_working are ONE phase.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch (the copilot process exists while the session dir still holds only workspace.yaml)

The delegation prompt drives the session ready → working (spec bullet 1), and it STAYS working across the subagent's lifetime — it neither settles to ready nor drops into waiting while the child runs (spec bullet 4). subagent.started/subagent.completed are Skip=true and are not themselves state changes.
copilot PID bound to the real session (matched by cwd from session.start.data.context.cwd)
After the subagent reports back and the parent replies 'done', the explicit assistant.turn_end fires: working → ready (spec bullet 5 — only after the last child ends)
